question: When resistors are connected in series combination, then potential difference across each resistor will be :
solution:
The correct answer is __**Proportional to resistance**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When resistors are connected in series, the potential difference across each resistor is **proportional to its resistance**.
 
• In a series circuit, the same current flows through all the resistors.
 
• According to Ohm's Law, V=IR where V is the potential difference, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• Since the current I is the same for all resistors in series, the potential difference VV" id="MathJax-Element-98-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V" id="MathJax-Element-14-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0"> V V across each resistor depends on its resistance R.
 
• Therefore, higher the resistance, higher the potential difference across that resistor in a series circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance is the sum of individual resistance: Rₜₒₜₐₗ=R₁+R₂+R₃+....
 
• The total potential difference across the series combination is the sum of the potential differences across each resistor: Vₜₒₜₐₗ=V₁+V₂+V₃+....
 
• This characteristic is useful in designing circuits where specific voltage drops are required across different components.
